sources.quote: The Clerk of Court is further directed to transfer this action to the United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York.
sources.searcher_note: Docket for Liotti v. Jet Blue Airways, 1:17-cv-00838: transfer order signed by Judge Colleen McMahon 2017-02-07, five days after filing. Case went to EDNY as 2:17-cv-00836 (Judge Vitaliano; judgment for JetBlue 2018). No mention of spouse, fees, or recusal.

sources.outlet: FindLaw (7th Cir. opinion, Specht v. Leinenweber, No. 10-2823)
sources.quote: Had he done so, the case would not have been assigned to Judge Leinenweber, whose wife (Lynn Martin) is a member of AT & T's board of directors.
sources.searcher_note: Same judge and same spouse-director mechanism, but the company is AT&T, not P&G; opinion says the court's automated conflict system blocks AT&T cases from his docket under 28 U.S.C. 455(b)(5)(i). Does not mention Gardner v. P&G.

sources.quote: In an examination of more than 1,200 federal judges and state supreme court justices, ProPublica, in partnership with student journalists at Boston University, found dozens of judges
sources.searcher_note: Pattern: judges not recusing when family members have financial ties to parties (Vitter, Canady, Tunheim). No spouse-corporate-director example; does not name McMahon, Leinenweber, JetBlue or P&G. ABA Journal rewrite (2024-07-19) not recorded.

notes: No source found that reports either judge presiding over a case against their spouse's company. No docket or page found for Gardner v. Procter & Gamble, 1:09-cv-06690 (govinfo and search returned other Gardner cases). Search results note Lynn Martin sat on P&G's board 1994-2010 (Wikipedia) and JetBlue's 2008 release names Frank Sica vice-chairman; neither mentions the cases. McMahon-Sica conflict claims found only on self-published Medium/Scribd/X pages by a litigant (not recorded, not news). CourtListener and Justia copies of the Specht opinion blocked fetch; FindLaw copy works. Other pattern coverage exists (Floodlight/Type Investigations/WWNO 2026-04-13 on Louisiana oil-case judges' financial ties) but it covers stock and law-firm ties, not spouse board seats. No coverage after 2026-06-30 found.
